findings.rationale: From round 11 NE's feature distribution jumps (AgeGroup, GenHlth, HighBP shift about 2 federation SDs, versus about 0 before round 10). Its update norm jumps from about 1.3-1.6x the median to about 2.9x, and its cosine to the median update turns negative from round 11 (about -0.06 falling to -0.74). Its final-round local performance is miscalibrated (CITL +0.075, ECE z=+4.8) while AUC is in the normal range. Feature outliers (HighBP low tail, GenHlth high tail) are far beyond its own noise. This pattern is consistent with a distribution shift from round 11 on, not with a static data or poisoning fault.

UT's feature shift appears at round 11 (AgeGroup, then GenHlth/HighBP; shift_sd about 1.8-2.3 from round 11 on, versus 0 before). Its update norm is about 2.1x the median with a strongly negative minimum cosine (-0.70, flagged z=-3.7), and its final-round CITL is +0.064 with ECE z=+4.2. Its HighBP low tail and GenHlth high tail are outliers in feature_summary. Same onset and direction as the other shifted clients.

WA's feature distribution shifts at round 11 (GenHlth then HighBP/AgeGroup; shift_sd about 1.8-2.1 from round 11 on, versus about 0 before). Its update norm jumps from about 2.2-2.8x to 3.6x the median at round 11 and its cosine falls from 0.79 to 0.06 and then negative (-0.81 by round 20). Final-round CITL is +0.067 with ECE z=+4.5 and a flagged mean_shift_sd z=+17.8. AUC is normal. This matches a drift fault starting at round 11.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views (updates, local performance, drift, feature tails, subgroup outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (NE, UT, WA) show the same signature from round 11: a roughly 2 SD feature shift (AgeGroup, GenHlth, HighBP), an update-norm jump, negative cosine to the median update, and miscalibration at the final round (CITL about +0.065 to +0.075) with normal AUC. I classified this as drift with onset round 11. Other flags were weak or inconsistent: GU (small n=708, CITL and norm flags that did not persist across rounds), SC/WY/NH/MT subgroup and BMI/sentinel-type outliers (small-n noise, no consistent under-diagnosis or missing-artefact pattern), and no AUC drops that would indicate label noise. The remaining budget was exhausted (0 left), so the attribution-churn check and some lower-priority confirmations were not run. Confidence in the three drift findings is reasonably high but not certain.
